_comment: Artifact pins in the signed public/api/identity.json that were ALREADY broken when scripts/check-identity-pins.sh was introduced (2026-08-06). This file is an acknowledgement list, not a mute button: a tracked-class entry suppresses the gate only while BOTH pinned_sha256 and observed_sha256 still hold. Re-sign the manifest or edit the artifact again and the entry stops applying, so the break is reported as new. Stream-class entries are documentation only - they never gate anything, because a push-owned feed is rewritten by host cron on its own cadence and its pin is stale by construction. Every entry here is a C4 (stop pinning moving streams / re-issue on artifact change) work item.

c4_status._comment: C4 landed in the GENERATOR, not in the signed artifact. scripts/operator-local/gen-identity.sh no longer pins any kind=stream publication (2026-08-14). Nothing about the manifest currently SERVED changes until the operator re-runs the generator: identity.json is signed with a passphrase-protected ed25519 key held only on the operator's Mac, so no automation and no reviewer can re-issue it. The three entries below are therefore kept rather than deleted early — but read what_these_three_entries_describe first: they record the 2026-08-04 manifest, NOT the bytes served today.

what_these_three_entries_describe._comment: Corrected 2026-08-14 after measurement. An earlier draft of this block claimed the three entries 'still describe the live signed bytes exactly'. That was false, and the falsehood mattered: docs/IDENTITY_VERIFICATION.md points third parties at this file.
what_these_three_entries_describe.finding: known_broken[*].pinned_sha256 are the pins of the manifest signed 2026-08-04 (90bcdd9), not of the manifest served today (2d69395, generated_at 2026-08-06T05:31:44Z). recorded_against.identity_generated_at names the 08-06 manifest and is inconsistent with them; it is corrected here rather than rewritten in place.
what_these_three_entries_describe.evidence: repo public/api/identity.json and the served copy are byte-identical (sha256 8018f2b1eb4eeb12…, both measured 2026-08-14). Its pins are evidence 5173ba5a…, uptime-cycles e47eb045…, validator 21640cd0…. This file records pinned_sha256 evidence 12a6d860…, uptime-cycles f021ab89…, validator 86e0fedd… — all three are 90bcdd9's values. For evidence and uptime-cycles the observed_sha256 recorded here (5173ba5a… / e47eb045…) is what the 08-06 re-issue then pinned; validator's observed_sha256 (1e3e0a75…) matches neither side, because that feed had moved again before it was re-signed. That divergence is itself the argument for C4.
what_these_three_entries_describe.why_they_are_still_kept: They are a true record of a real state, and the defect class they name — a signed pin over a push-owned feed — is still present in the served manifest, merely with different digits. Deleting them before that condition is gone would erase the acknowledgement while the thing acknowledged is still there.
what_these_three_entries_describe.why_the_values_are_not_updated: scripts/check-identity-pins.sh suppresses a tracked-class mismatch only while BOTH pinned_sha256 and observed_sha256 still hold, so editing those values edits gate behaviour. These three are class=stream and gate nothing either way, so there is no benefit to weigh against touching a suppression record.

c4_status.retire_when: the next gen-identity.sh issuance lands (scheduled: the 2026-09-04 cycle transition, phase 2). At that point public/api/identity.json carries no sha256 for any of these three paths, the pin ids below stop existing, and all three entries MUST be deleted from known_broken in the same commit that lands the new manifest. docs/CYCLE_GATE.md carries this as a numbered step.
c4_status.gate_effect_of_keeping_them: none. scripts/check-identity-pins.sh only emits OBSOLETE-BASELINE for class=tracked entries (see its section 4); a class=stream entry can neither suppress nor raise anything, in either mode.

This entry retires then - see c4_status.retire_when.
